Catholic Studies Program to host lecture on Archbishop Sheen's theology of the Crucifixion
A. M. Egan
The Catholic Studies Program announced on Aug. 26 that it will present "I Thirst: Archbishop Fulton Sheen's Theology of the Crucifixion" with Edmund M. Lazzari, Ph.L., STL (Cand.), Ph.D., at 2 p.m. on Wednesday, September 16 in Mooney Hall Room 339 (the CORE center).
The event is co-sponsored by The University Core and Campus Ministry. According to the announcement, soon-to-be-Blessed Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen delivered special sermons on the Cross of Christ every Good Friday for over thirty-five years. His reflections are described as deeply rooted in Biblical teachings concerning Christ's life, passion, death, and resurrection.
As U.S. director for the Society for the Propagation of the Faith, Archbishop Sheen reportedly witnessed global suffering firsthand and personally endured heart issues, becoming the oldest person to undergo open heart surgery in 1975. The program states that "Thoroughly immersed in the Scriptures, Archbishop Sheen sees all of the suffering of the world united to the Cross of Christ, making Christ the truly universal redeemer through His Death and Resurrection." It adds that his theology centers redemption as "the center of all human history," emphasizing inclusivity with "Christ's arms are open on the Cross to embrace the whole world."
Edmund M. Lazzari is an assistant professor of Catholic Studies and assistant coordinator of External Programs for Duquesne University's Department of Catholic Studies. He specializes in theology-science dialogue, Christian-Muslim dialogue, and Catholic speculative theology, with research interests including theological metaphysics and Christology.
Lazzari has published articles on topics such as artificial intelligence’s theological implications, beauty in sacred music, Aristotle’s role in Islamic metaphysics, patristic angelology related to Tolkien’s works, and Catholic perspectives on intelligent extraterrestrial life across various academic journals. He is also author of two books: Why Nature Matters: Unlocking Catholic Doctrine through Commonsense Philosophy and Miracles in Said Nursi and Thomas Aquinas: Non-Noninterventionist Approaches to Divine Action and the Sciences (Routledge, 2024).
The event is free and open to members of the public.
